friction.title: The --agent flag of agent send names the target, but names the sender in inbox send
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-21, the manager of hive sent an instruction to worker
`t2-worker-1` with `hive agent send --agent t2-worker-1 --agent manager-hive
--wait TEXT`. The manager added the second `--agent` to name itself as the
sender, as `hive inbox send` requires. In `hive agent send`, `--agent` names
the target. The second value replaced the first with no error. Hive sent the
instruction to the manager pane, and the worker did not get it. The `--wait`
call then waited on the busy manager until the tool timeout. The workaround
was to send again with one `--agent`. The manager instructions list both
commands with `--agent NAME`, with two different meanings.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. As a manager, run `hive agent send --agent WORKER --agent MANAGER TEXT`.
2. Hive sends TEXT to the manager pane, not to the worker. Hive shows no
   error for the repeated flag.
3. Compare `hive inbox send --to coordinator TEXT --agent NAME`, where
   `--agent` names the sender.

friction.title: An agent can send a user chat message through the TUI
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-20 at 14:4x UTC, worker t89-worker-1 (task 89-screen-board-audit)
ran the TUI in its own pane to audit the screens. It pressed `i` on the Chat
screen and typed screen keys. The TUI sent "278" with `hive chat send`, and the
coordinator got `⬢ user: 278` (chat record c1). A message with `⬢ user:`
carries the authority of the user. The coordinator treated it as a message from
the user and replied (c2).

`hive chat send` refuses a caller that passes `--agent`. The TUI does not pass
it, and nothing checks where the TUI runs. Thus each agent that can run `hive`
can make a message with the authority of the user. Only the report from the
manager showed the true source.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. In the pane of a worker, run bare `hive`.
2. On screen 1, press `i`, type text, and press Enter.
3. The coordinator pane gets `⬢ user: TEXT`, and `hive chat log` shows a user
   record.

**Fix and remaining gap:**
Task 94-chat-user-only makes `chat.Send` refuse a caller with `--agent`, a
caller in the pane of a live agent, a caller with a working directory below
`projects/`, and a caller in the workspace of a live manager, worker, or
verifier. The TUI passes its pane and working directory. A gap stays open: an
agent can open a tab in the hive session workspace with a working directory
outside `projects/`, and that tab can still send a user chat message.

friction.title: A completed task cannot be reopened or edited
friction.body:
**Summary:**
`hive task reopen` accepts a verified task, and `hive task edit` accepts a
created or assigned task. A completed task accepts neither. On 2026-10-20 the
repair worker of 85-logs-screen completed Repair 2. Before a verifier ran,
task 83 landed on `dev`, and the branch got a new conflict in
`internal/tui/tui.go`. The manager could not add Repair 3 to the brief or
reopen the task. It had to spawn a verifier only to record a fail, so that the
task went back to `assigned`.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Run `hive task complete` on a task.
2. Run `hive task reopen --task ID --reason TEXT`: `invalid transition:
   completed -> reopen`.
3. Run `hive task edit --task ID --brief FILE`: `edit needs created or
   assigned`.

**Recurrence 2026-10-20 (stenographer 63-hub-sessions):** the worker
completed while tasks 61 and 72 landed on `dev`, and the branch got content
conflicts in `cli/hub/app.py` and `cli/hub/services.py`. `hive agent spawn
--role worker` refused (`task is completed`) and `hive task reopen` refused
(`completed -> reopen`). The manager again spawned a verifier only to record
the conflict as a failed check. Parallel tasks that touch one shared file make
this common.

**Related:** `hive worktree remove` on a task whose worktree is already
removed fails with `worktree check: start git: fork/exec /usr/bin/git: no such
file or directory`. Git exists. The working directory of the Git call is the
removed worktree. The message does not say that the worktree is gone.

**Recurrence 2026-10-20 (stenographer hub board tasks 109-111):** four tasks
ran in parallel and all edited `cli/hub/app.py`. Each landing (112, 115, 109,
116, 110) gave the others new conflicts. Tasks 110 and 111 each needed two
extra verifier runs only to record "dev merge needed", then a merge-only
worker; 111 also conflicted in `site/index.html`. That is six verifier and
worker cycles spent on conflicts. A verifier-free path for a completed task
that only needs a dev merge would remove most of them.

friction.title: The local gate does not run the module tidy check of CI
friction.body:
**Summary:**
The CI job `gate` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `go mod tidy` and
`git diff --exit-code -- go.mod go.sum`. The gate in `AGENTS.md`, the worker
skill, and the verifier skill has four commands and no tidy check. Task
79-tui-shell added a direct import of `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi`, but
`go.mod` kept it as indirect. CI on `dev` failed from merge 7204d699 to
7def7814 (run 39388680419). Each worker and verifier gate passed. The manager
landed waves B and C on a red CI, because no step of the flow reads the CI
result.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. In a task, import a package that `go.mod` lists as indirect.
2. Run the four gate commands of `AGENTS.md`: all pass.
3. Run `go mod tidy && git diff --exit-code -- go.mod go.sum`: it fails.
4. Land the task on `dev`: the CI job `gate` fails.

friction.title: Bare hive in a scratch home starts real tabs
friction.decision: Task 8-no-startup adds the opt-in switch --no-startup and HIVE_NO_STARTUP=1
friction.body:
**Summary:**
Bare hive runs the startup of G9: in herdr, it starts a
coordinator and a supervisor in their own tabs when they are
missing. A worker or verifier that runs bare hive with
HIVE_HOME set to a scratch home gets no live coordinator and a
stale supervisor claim, so each run starts a new coordinator
tab and a new hive supervise process in the caller workspace.

**Reproduction:**
1. In a herdr pane, make a scratch home with a marker.
2. Run HIVE_HOME=<scratch> hive and quit the TUI.
3. herdr tab list shows a new coordinator and supervisor tab.

**Occurrences:**
2026-10-20  worker of 101 left 4 supervisors, 8 tabs
2026-10-20  t91-worker-1 closed the user TUI tab
2026-10-21  third scratch hive tab leak

**Mitigation:**
Task 8-no-startup of feature tui-v2 adds the switch
hive --no-startup and the variable HIVE_NO_STARTUP=1, from
decision 34 of the spec. With either one, bare hive opens the
TUI. It makes no tab, starts no coordinator and no supervisor,
and does not rename the tab.
The worker skill and the verifier skill tell each agent to run
bare hive only with the switch or the variable.
The entry stays open: the switch is opt-in, and automatic
detection of a scratch home is out of scope.
Refer to the spec README of tui-v2, decision 34, and the
worker and verifier skills.

friction.title: Each brief copy row conflicts in the STE baseline
friction.body:
**Summary:**
Each spec task adds one row with 0 for its brief copy to
`testdata/ste-baseline.json`. Two tasks that run in parallel add rows at the
same place, so the second land fails with a merge conflict. Each conflict
needs a reopen, a repair worker, and a new verifier. On 2026-10-20 this
occurred for 85-logs-screen (repair 2) and 89-screen-board-audit (repair 1
after 94-chat-user-only landed). Wave D has ten parallel tasks.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Create two spec tasks from the same `dev` commit.
2. Let each worker add its brief copy row to `testdata/ste-baseline.json`.
3. Land the first task.
4. Run `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/dev origin/task/<second>`: a
   conflict in `testdata/ste-baseline.json`.

**More occurrences (2026-10-20):** 93-ci-test-fixes (with 88), and
100-no-backgrounds and 97-friction-detail-panel after 93 and 98 landed. The
manager repairs one task at a time, because a parallel repair conflicts again
after the first land. Possible fixes: one baseline file for each task brief
copy, or a test that gives each brief copy a baseline of 0 when no row exists.

**Related (2026-10-20):** a worker rewords its brief copy when the copy fails
`TestSTERatchet`. A later `hive task edit` (for a repair) copies the manager
brief into the worktree again. That undoes the rewording, and the repair
worker gets the same STE failure. This occurred for 93 and 97.

**Again (2026-10-21):** goal `g2-tui-v2` ran `8-no-startup` and `9-cellgrid`
at the same time. Task 8 landed first. `hive land` for task 9 then failed with
a merge conflict in `testdata/ste-baseline.json`. The manager reopened task 9,
a worker merged `dev`, and a second verifier ran. The conflict added one
worker and one verifier. CP5 task `6-cp5-record` had the same conflict after
`13-remove-bootstrap` landed.

friction.title: A failed verification is lost when the next verification passes
friction.body:
**Summary:**
`verification_history` gets an entry only from `hive task reopen`. After a
verify fail, the manager edits the brief and spawns a repair worker without a
reopen, because the task goes back to `assigned`. The next `hive task verify`
replaces `verification` with the pass, and the fail is gone from the record.
On 2026-10-20 task 79-tui-shell failed V1 with t79-verifier-1 and passed with
t79-verifier-2. Its record shows only the pass, and the new `VERIFIED.md`
replaced the old one. The Tasks screen (task 83) cannot show the repair
history that its design shows.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Run `hive task verify` with a fail on a completed task.
2. Complete the task again and run `hive task verify` with a pass.
3. Run `hive task show --json`: `verification_history` is empty.

friction.title: A brief tells a worker to read its inbox, but a worker has no inbox
friction.body:
**Summary:**
The Finish section of each wave D brief says "Read only your own inbox." The
worker skill does not name an inbox command. A worker has no inbox: on
2026-10-20 t91-worker-1 ran `hive inbox --json --agent t91-worker-1 --all`
and got `role has no inbox: worker`. The worker then sent its completion
report to the coordinator, not to the manager. The manager gets messages to
a worker with `hive agent send`, so the brief line is wrong. Hive has no rule
that stops a worker from sending to the coordinator.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. As a worker, run `hive inbox --agent NAME --all`: `role has no inbox:
   worker`.
2. Run `hive inbox send --to coordinator TEXT --agent NAME`: the record is
   created, though the brief names the manager as the receiver.

friction.title: Claude Code in bypass mode still asks before a dangerous rm
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, verifier t44-verifier-1 (Claude Code, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`)
ran a command with `rm -rf $S/*`. Claude Code showed a dialog "Dangerous rm
operation on possibly-empty variable path" and waited, with an automatic deny
after about 2 minutes. The supervisor wrote a `blocked` record to the manager.
The manager denied the dialog. The verifier ran the step again without the rm
and recorded the verdict. The bypass flag does not stop this safety check.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a Claude Code verifier with hive (bypass flag on).
2. The agent runs `rm -rf $VAR/*` with a shell variable.
3. Claude Code shows the dangerous rm dialog. herdr reports `blocked`.

**Recurrence 2026-10-19 (qmeter):** verifier t52-verifier-1 hit the same
dialog on `rm -rf $S/*` in its scratchpad cleanup, chained after
`hive task verify` in one command. herdr reported `blocked`; the blocked
inbox record had no reason, so the manager had to read the pane with
`herdr pane read` to find it. The manager denied it and the verifier reran
`hive task verify` alone.

**Occurrence 2026-10-20:**
Verifier t81-verifier-2 ran `rm -f -- "$S"/*.txt` on its scratchpad in a
cleanup step, although its note said to avoid `rm` on an unquoted variable.
The same dialog showed. The manager denied it with `herdr pane send-keys
<pane> Escape`. A note in the verifier prompt does not stop the pattern.

**Recurrence 2026-10-20 (stenographer 108, 110):** t108-verifier-3 hit the
dialog on `rm -rf $S/*` in its final commit step, and t110-verifier-2 on
`rm -rf $S/$rev` before the manager's prompt arrived. The manager declined
with `herdr pane send-keys <pane> Down`, then `Return` (`Enter` did not
register). `hive agent send` refuses while the pane is blocked
(`agent_blocked`).

friction.title: No dashboard shows the agents, their lineage, their activity, and their tasks
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, the user asked the coordinator for a list of the work of each
active agent. The user cannot see this state easily. To answer, the
coordinator ran `hive agent list` and `hive task list` and joined the output
by hand. The data has these problems:

- `hive agent list` shows the name, the role, the project, the task, and the
  pane. It does not show the parent agent (lineage), if the agent is working,
  idle, or blocked, or the time since its last activity.
- `hive task list` shows `verified` for a landed task. The user cannot tell a
  landed task from a task that waits for a landing.
- The goal of a manager is only in the coordinator notes and in the inbox.
  No hive view shows it.
- Bare `hive` opens a TUI with only a header and the log view
  (`internal/tui/doc.go`).

The user wants a dashboard in the bare `hive` TUI, as btop and htop show
processes. It shows:

1. Each agent as a tree: the coordinator, then each manager, then the workers
   and the verifiers of that manager.
2. For each agent: the harness, the model, the state (working, idle, blocked,
   exited), the time since the last activity, and the pane.
3. For each manager: its project, its goal, and its tasks with their status
   and dependencies.
4. For each worker and verifier: its task, the task status, and the branch.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a manager. The manager spawns 2 workers.
2. Run bare `hive`. Only the header and the log view show.
3. Run `hive agent list`. No parent, no activity state, and no goal show.
4. Run `hive task list`. A landed task shows `verified`.

friction.title: Hive cannot spawn a reviewer or another one-off agent
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19 the coordinator needed a plan review of the hive TUI goal by
GPT 6.1 Sol before the goal went to the manager. `hive agent spawn` accepts
only the roles coordinator, supervisor, manager, worker, and verifier
(`internal/agent/register.go:162`). A worker or a verifier needs a task. A
plan review has no task. `hive agent spawn --role reviewer` fails with
"invalid role: reviewer".

The coordinator ran `pi -p` in a background shell instead. That run waited
for 39 minutes with no output, because pi showed its "Trust project
folder?" prompt and no person could see it. The coordinator then started pi
by hand in a new herdr tab with `herdr pane run`. Hive has no record of that
agent, so `hive agent list` does not show it, and the supervisor does not
watch it. The agent also stopped at the same trust prompt, which the user
must answer.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Run `hive agent spawn --role reviewer --project hive --pane PANE --harness pi --model MODEL`.
2. The command fails with "invalid role: reviewer".
3. Run `pi -p --model MODEL "PROMPT"` in the home with no TTY.
4. The process waits with no output and no CPU use, at the trust prompt.

**Takeover:**
The pi reviewer in the home root ran coordinator startup two times. The
first prompt was "Read FILE and do what it says". The second prompt also
said "you are a plan reviewer, not the coordinator". Each time it ran
`hive agent register --role coordinator`, which marked the live coordinator
stale, took the coordinator claim, and renamed the review tab to
`coordinator`. Nudges then went to the reviewer pane. It also read the
coordinator inbox and ran `hive doctor`. The real coordinator ran
`hive agent register --role coordinator` again to take back the claim. A
pi agent in a scratch directory outside the home, with the tools read,
grep, find, ls, and write, did not load `AGENTS.md` or the hive skills and
did the review only.

5. Start pi in the home root with a prompt that names another role.
6. pi runs `hive agent register --role coordinator` and takes the claim.

**Second occurrence (2026-10-21):** the user asked for a review of the
`tui-v2` spec draft by GPT 6.1 Sol in a pane that the user can see. Hive
still cannot spawn it: `hive agent spawn --role reviewer --pane w58:p7`
fails with "invalid role: reviewer" (`internal/agent/register.go:179`).
`hive agent spawn` has no free-text prompt flag. The coordinator made tab
`w58:t7` with `herdr tab create` and started pi there with
`herdr pane run`, with the prompt in a file. The tools were read, grep,
find, and ls only. With no bash tool, pi cannot run
`hive agent register`, so the coordinator claim stayed safe. Hive has no
record of this agent.

The reviewer finished, but it had no way to report back. Hive had no record
of it, so the supervisor sent no nudge, and the agent had no inbox and no
`hive` command. The coordinator did not know that the review was complete.
The user had to tell the coordinator. The coordinator then read the result
from the pane with `herdr pane read`.

**Third occurrence (2026-10-21):** the coordinator ran six review passes of
the `general-agent` spec by GPT 6.1 Sol in tab `w58:t8`, started by hand
with `herdr pane run`. The tools were read, grep, find, and ls only. The
coordinator sent each later pass as a new prompt with `herdr pane run` into
the same pi pane. To know when a pass was complete, the coordinator ran
`herdr agent wait PANE --until working`, then
`herdr agent wait PANE --until idle --until done --until blocked`, in a
background shell. The wait gave a correct completion signal for each pass.
The coordinator then read the result with `herdr pane read`. Hive still had
no record of the agent. The spec `general-agent` (goal `g3-general-agent`)
plans the fix.

**Occurrences:**
2026-10-19  plan review by pi waited 39 minutes at the trust prompt
2026-10-19  pi reviewer took the coordinator claim two times

friction.title: A supervisor nudge splits a message that the user types
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, between 02:40 and 02:45, the user typed (by speech-to-text
paste) 3 messages to the coordinator. The supervisor sent a nudge to the
coordinator pane while each message was in the prompt. The nudge text
"⬢ hive: N new inbox record(s), run: hive inbox" went into the prompt after
the partial text, and the nudge submitted the prompt. The coordinator got a
cut message, for example "For agents working, I am interested in a
tree/lineage type for⬢ hive: 3 new inbox records, run: hive inbox". The user
had to send the rest again. This occurred 3 times in about 5 minutes, while
the managers sent many records.

The supervisor does not check if the prompt of the pane has text before it
sends the nudge. A nudge for the coordinator is the most likely to collide,
because the user types in that pane.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Start `hive supervise`.
2. In the coordinator pane, type a partial message. Do not submit it.
3. Make a manager send a record to the coordinator inbox.
4. The nudge text goes after the partial text, and the prompt is submitted.

friction.title: A new task can go only in a feature that has a README
friction.body:
**Summary:**
After the spec migration (task 48), only `hive-v1` has
`.hive/spec/<feature>/README.md`. `hive task create` without `--spec` needs
that README on the base branch. On 2026-10-19 the manager made task
70-spec-allowlist, a fix to the H2 spec layout. Its feature is
`home-spec-planning`, but that feature has no README. The manager put the task
in `hive-v1` to start it. Until each feature has a README from its spec task,
a manager must put new tasks in `hive-v1` or make a spec task first.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Run `hive task create --project hive --feature home-spec-planning --title T --slug s --brief FILE`.
2. It fails: the README is missing on the base branch.
3. Run the same command with `--feature hive-v1`. It succeeds.

friction.title: The verifier skill does not give the path of VERIFIED.md
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, verifier t36-verifier-1 (Claude Opus 5.5) of
36-nudge-no-home wrote `VERIFIED.md` at the root of the checkout. All earlier
tasks put it in `evidence/<task-id>/VERIFIED.md`. The skill
`.agents/skills/hive-verifier/SKILL.md` names `VERIFIED.md` but gives no path.
`hive task verify` accepted the root file. A root `VERIFIED.md` on `dev` causes
a conflict with the next verifier that does the same. The workaround was
`hive task reopen`, a repair worker to move the file, and a fresh verifier.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a verifier for a completed task.
2. The verifier reads the skill and writes `VERIFIED.md` at the checkout root.
3. Run `hive task verify`. It records a pass with no path check.

friction.title: The worker skill gate adds golangci-lint that the project gate does not have
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, in project qmeter, workers t50-worker-1, t51-worker-2 and
t53-worker-1 each stopped before `hive task complete` and asked the manager
for a waiver. The hive-worker gate runs `golangci-lint run ./...`. qmeter's
`AGENTS.md` and the briefs name only gofmt, vet, race tests and the
next-version test. `dev` already has 27 to 33 golangci-lint findings, and
`--new-from-rev=dev` reports 0 for each task. Each stop cost one manager
round trip. Also, a `blocked` inbox record carries only the text `blocked`,
not the reason.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Use a project whose gate in `AGENTS.md` has no golangci-lint, and whose
   base branch has lint findings.
2. Spawn a pi worker for a task of that project.
3. The worker runs the hive-worker gate, sees golangci-lint fail on
   unchanged files, and asks the manager instead of completing.

friction.title: A stale coordinator record blocks bare hive startup
friction.decision: Task 2 makes bare hive check the coordinator pane at startup, and task 3 adds the r restart on the Agents screen
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-20, the coordinator record had status `live` and named pane
`w2T:p1`. Herdr reported `pane_not_found` for that pane. Bare `hive` checked
only the record status. It did not start a new coordinator. Chat delivery
failed with `agent_not_found`. The supervisor subscribed to the missing pane
and exited with `pane_not_found`. The workaround was to confirm that the pane
was gone, mark the stale coordinator record `exited`, and start bare `hive`
again. Startup must check the recorded Herdr pane before it treats a
coordinator as live.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Leave a coordinator agent record with status `live` after its Herdr pane
   closes.
2. Run bare `hive` in a Herdr pane of the home. Hive does not start a new
   coordinator.
3. Send a chat message in the TUI. Delivery reports `agent_not_found`.
4. Run `hive doctor`. It reports that the supervisor is down. The supervisor
   log reports `pane_not_found` for the stale coordinator pane.

**Plan (approved by the user 2026-10-21):**
The user asked for a TUI action that restarts the coordinator or the
supervisor, and for stale records to stop blocking startup. This plan also
removes the manual workaround in `supervisor-runs-stale-binary.md`.

1. Bare `hive` counts a `live` coordinator record as dead when its Herdr pane
   is gone. It starts a new coordinator. Register marks the old record
   `stale` with the existing claim rule.
2. The coordinator and supervisor records show that bare `hive` started them.
   Restart can then close their old panes under the AGENTS.md rule.
3. On the Agents screen, the user selects the coordinator or supervisor node
   and presses `r`. Hive asks for confirmation only when the target is live.
   A dead or stale target restarts at once.
4. A coordinator restart closes the old pane, opens a new `coordinator` tab,
   and starts the configured harness with the startup prompt, as bare `hive`
   does.
5. A supervisor restart closes its pane through Herdr, opens a new
   `supervisor` tab, and runs `hive supervise`. The abrupt SIGHUP exit is
   accepted.
6. Old records get the correct status (`stale` or `stopped`). Hive keeps the
   files. `h` hides them. Hive deletes no record.
7. The TUI header marks the supervisor `old` when it runs an older binary than
   the installed `hive`, with the hint `r to restart`.

Delivery: task 1 is steps 1 and 2. Task 2 is steps 3 to 7 and starts after
task 1 lands. The manager lands each verified task on `dev` under the
2026-10-18 grant.

friction.title: The supervisor keeps running an old hive binary
friction.decision: Task 3 adds r restart and an old-binary mark
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, the supervisor (pid 1718014) started at 13:22
from the hive binary of 72a33b5b. The managers rebuilt
~/go/bin/hive after waves 2, 3, and 4. The supervisor kept the
old code, so the wave 2 change was not live. hive doctor
reported the supervisor as live and did not compare its binary
with the installed one.

**Resolved by:**
3-tui-restart  merge 3ccd93fb

**Reproduction:**
1. Start hive supervise.
2. Land a change to the supervisor and run go install or
   go build for hive.
3. Run hive doctor. It reports the old supervisor as live.
4. Trigger the changed behavior. The supervisor uses the old
   code.
No skill told an agent to restart the supervisor after a
rebuild.

friction.title: A feature spec task cannot start in a repository that ignores .hive/spec/
friction.decision: Fixed in 70-spec-allowlist (e1276caa): a spec task worktree stages the brief with git add -f and reports allowlist_needed; the spec task commits the .gitignore rules.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
Since the spec migration (task 48), `hive task create` needs `--feature`,
and `hive worktree create` writes the brief to
`.hive/spec/<feature>/tasks/<id>/brief.md` in the project worktree. When the
project `.gitignore` does not allow `.hive/spec/`, the worktree create fails:
"path is ignored ... The .gitignore of the repo must allow .hive/spec/". The
only way to allow the path is a source change, which needs a task and a
worktree. So the first spec task of such a project cannot start. A manager
never edits a source file, so the manager is blocked. It occurred once, in
project `stenographer`, whose `.gitignore` ignores every path that it does not
allow.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Use a project whose `.gitignore` starts with `*` and does not allow `.hive/`.
2. Run `hive task create --project ID --feature F --spec --title T --slug S --brief FILE`. It succeeds.
3. Run `hive worktree create --task ID-S`. It fails with "path is ignored".
4. Run `hive task create` without `--feature`. It fails with "feature requires a value".

friction.title: store.List skips an agent record with a key longer than 18 characters
friction.decision: Task 101-store-list-long-keys: List and ListIn keep each valid store segment of any length (merge e6f70c2f).
friction.body:
**Summary:**
`store.List` in `internal/lib/store/store.go` skips each record file whose ID
fails `records.ValidID`, which allows at most 18 characters. Agent keys such as
`manager-stenographer-g7` (23 characters) are valid agent keys, so a caller
that lists agents with `store.List` loses them with no error. `agent.List`
shows them. On 2026-10-20 the verifier of task 81-agents-screen found that the
new Agents screen missed `manager-stenographer-g1` to `-g7` on the real home
while the header counted them. Repair 1 of task 81 moves the screen to
`agent.List`. The silent skip stays for each other caller of `store.List`.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Register a manager for a project with an ID of 12 or more characters, so
   its key is longer than 18 characters.
2. List the `agents` kind with `store.List`.
3. The record is not in the result, and no error shows.

friction.title: A verified task that never landed cannot be cancelled
friction.decision: Task 105 lets cancel close a verified task with no pushed delivery, and lets land record a branch that is already on the base
friction.body:
**Summary:**
`hive task cancel` refuses a task with status `verified`: `invalid transition:
verified -> cancel`. A verified task that will not land stays open, gives
ghosts on the Agents screen, and keeps a worktree that doctor reports. On
2026-10-20 the user cancelled `10-pr47-final`. The manager ran `hive task
reopen` (verified to assigned) and then `hive task cancel` as a workaround.
The worktree held only untracked evidence, so `hive worktree remove` refused
it as dirty. The manager copied the evidence to
`.hive/tmp/archive/10-pr47-final/` and used `--force`.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Take a task with status `verified` that has no delivery.
2. Run `hive task cancel --task ID --reason R`: `invalid transition:
   verified -> cancel`.
3. Run `hive task reopen --task ID --reason R`, then `hive task cancel`: the
   task is cancelled.

**Second case (2026-10-20):** stenographer `45-ci-fix` has status
`verified` and a delivery with commit `4a94e73` and `pushed: false`. The
commit is on `origin/dev` and `origin/main`. The record does not read landed.
`hive task cancel` gives the same refusal. A `hive land --mode merge` for a
task with a delivery commit skips the merge and only pushes the base branch
(`internal/land/merge.go`, the `retry` path). The local `dev` of stenographer
is equal to `origin/dev`, so that push has nothing to send and sets `pushed`
to true. This is a workaround, not a clear command: no command records a land
for a commit that is already on the base, and no command cancels a verified
task. Same family as `completed-task-cannot-reopen`.

friction.title: An agent spawn can skip the first prompt
friction.decision: Fixed in 28-first-prompt-fix (642fe78d): the first prompt uses the herdr prompt wait until working or blocked, with one retry on a stall. The user accepts the risk of a duplicate prompt.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
A released-shell event could change the new agent record to
`exited` before `agent.start` returned. The agent then ran without its first
prompt. The `starting` status keeps the supervisor from treating this event as
an exit. Fix commit: `c7b2566`.

On 2026-10-19, the manager spawned worker `t11-worker-1` with
`hive agent spawn --role worker` and no `--pane`. The spawn printed
`prompted agent` and `agent t11-worker-1 live`. Pi did not get the first
prompt. The pane stayed idle at context 0k. The workaround was
`herdr pane send-text`, then `herdr pane send-keys Enter`.

**Merged text from the `agent_not_ready` entry:**
On 2026-10-19, `hive agent send` to a Pi agent spawned with
`--pane` failed with `agent_not_ready` two times. This task records the issue.
It does not fix it.

**Report 2026-10-19:**
Report: `.hive/tmp/reports/first-prompt-skip.md` in the home (task
21-first-prompt-report). Cause: `promptStarted` in
`internal/agent/spawn_worker.go` accepts `idle` as proof of delivery before it
compares `state_change_seq` and `revision`. For all four wave 4 worker spawns,
the state after `agent.prompt` was `idle` with the same seq and revision as the
baseline, so hive logged `prompted agent` and skipped the retry. herdr
`agent.prompt` success proves only that the text and Enter were written. Why Pi
dropped those prompts stays unknown. A live test showed that an accepted prompt
can also look like an unchanged `idle` at first, so an immediate retry can send
a duplicate. Proposed fixes: use the herdr prompt wait as delivery evidence and
retry after a bounded stall result; or accept `idle` only after a seq or
revision change, with a bounded observation window.

**Probe 2026-10-19:**
Report: `.hive/tmp/reports/prompt-wait-probe.md` in the home (task
26-prompt-wait-probe). Each case ran 3 times with
`herdr agent prompt PANE TEXT --wait --until working --until blocked --timeout 10000`.
A Pi prompt into a new `herdr worktree create` pane returned
`agent_prompt_stalled` after 5.3 s in 3 of 3 runs, with no prompt in the pane.
One fresh Pi in a plain scratch workspace also stalled (1 of 3). Each retry
returned `working` and showed the prompt one time. Fast-finish prompts returned
`working`, then `done`, with no false stall. A Claude trust dialog returned
`agent_blocked` in 0.001 s and typed nothing. Claude never dropped a prompt.
Verdict: option 1 (the herdr prompt wait as delivery evidence, then a retry
after a stall) was safe in all 24 runs. It is not proven for an accepted prompt
that stays idle for more than 5 s; a retry could then send a duplicate.

**Resolution 2026-10-19:**
Fixed in 28-first-prompt-fix, landed at 642fe78d. Each spawn sends its first
prompt with the `agent.prompt` wait until `working` or `blocked` and a bounded
timeout. On `agent_prompt_stalled`, hive retries one time. A second stall fails
the spawn and names the agent and the cause. On `agent_blocked`, hive sends no
more text. The unchanged-`idle` delivery check is gone. The live check spawned
three Pi workers into new worktrees, and each one got its first prompt with no
hand resend.

Accepted risk: when an accepted prompt stays idle longer than the herdr wait
window, hive retries and the agent can get the prompt two times. The user
accepts this risk. Hive has no pane-read guard against it.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a verifier with `--pane`.
2. Read the verifier pane.
3. Check that the first prompt is absent.
4. Send the prompt with `hive agent send`.
5. On 2026-10-19, spawn worker `t11-worker-1` with
   `hive agent spawn --role worker` and no `--pane`.
6. Check the output for `prompted agent` and `agent t11-worker-1 live`.
7. Read the Pi pane. It is idle at context 0k and has no first prompt.
8. Run `herdr pane send-text`, then `herdr pane send-keys Enter`.

Later on 2026-10-19, the first prompt was absent again for `t12-worker-1`,
`t11-verifier-1` (Claude, with `--pane`), `t11-worker-2` (with `--pane`), and
`t13-worker-1`. Each spawn printed `agent NAME live`. The first prompt arrived
for `t11-verifier-2` and `t12-verifier-1`, both Pi verifiers with no
`--pane`. The same workaround applied each time.

**Reproduction steps from the `agent_not_ready` entry:**
1. Spawn a Pi agent with `hive agent spawn --pane`.
2. Run `hive agent send` for that agent.
3. The command returns `agent_not_ready` (observed two times on 2026-10-19).

friction.title: Any agent can read and consume the inbox of another role
friction.decision: Fixed in 15-inbox-ownership (1d97f21f): only the owner's read marks records read. The coordinator can read a manager inbox and marks nothing. Any other caller gets an error that names the owner.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, verifier `t12-verifier-1` ran
`hive inbox --role manager-hive` at 12:46:30. That command marked record 66
(`verified` for 12-friction-log) as read. The supervisor then did not nudge
the manager, and the landing waited until the coordinator saw the record.
`hive inbox --role` accepts any role from any agent. The workaround is a
sentence in each brief that tells the agent to read only its own inbox.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a verifier for a task of project `hive`.
2. In the verifier pane, run `hive inbox --role manager-hive`.
3. Check that the command prints and marks the unread manager records.
4. Check that the supervisor sends no nudge to the manager for them.

friction.title: An exited agent name blocks reuse
friction.decision: Fixed in 19-worker-respawn (78381ba1): with no --name, hive picks the next free name tNN-ROLE-N.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
An exited agent name blocks a later spawn with `agent exists`.
Each retry needs a new agent name.

Resolution: Live check 2026-10-19: after a verify fail on 18-task-reopen, `hive agent spawn --role worker --task 18-task-reopen` with no `--name` and no `--pane` picked `t18-worker-2`, set it as the acting agent, and reopened the task workspace `wDJ` on the same worktree.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn an agent with the name `NAME`.
2. Let the agent exit.
3. Spawn another agent with the name `NAME`.
4. Check that hive returns `agent exists`.

friction.title: Full Pi worktree, agent, and delivery bootstrap flow is missing
friction.decision: Stale: `hive worktree` and `hive agent spawn/send/stop` exist.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
The full Pi worktree, agent, and delivery bootstrap flow still
lacks T09, T10, T12, and T18. The coordinator dispatches work by hand with
`herdr worktree` and `herdr agent` commands. This manual dispatch is the current
workaround. No runtime task or agent record simulates a missing capability.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Run `herdr worktree --help`. It lists `list`, `create`, `open`, and `remove`.
   The hive `worktree` command does not exist.
2. Run `herdr agent --help`. It lists `start`, `prompt`, `wait`, and related
   commands. The hive `agent spawn`, `agent send`, and `agent stop` commands do
   not exist.
3. The safe probe output is in
   `.hive/tmp/coordinator/reports/later-fix-land-01-captures/herdr-help-probes.txt`.

friction.title: An idle session burns tokens on supervisor nudges
friction.decision: Fixed in 16-quiet-no-nudge (848ef0b7): an unread quiet record never causes a nudge.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, with all tasks landed and both managers on hold,
the supervisor kept the coordinator awake. Each idle manager writes a `quiet`
record to the coordinator inbox every ten minutes. The supervisor types a
nudge into the coordinator pane for each unread record. Each nudge costs one
coordinator turn, which costs tokens, and a user who is away pays for it. The
coordinator's own file watch doubled the cost before it was stopped. The
workaround was to stop both managers and the supervisor by hand. Hive has no
hush mode: a state in which the supervisor holds routine kinds (`quiet`,
`completed`, `verified`) and nudges only for `blocked`, `exited`,
`unresolved`, and urgent messages. The firstmate `/quiet` mode is the model.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn two managers with no goals. Leave the coordinator idle.
2. Wait more than ten minutes.
3. Each manager writes a `quiet` record. The supervisor types
   `hive: 1 new inbox record, run: hive --home ... inbox` into the coordinator
   pane for each one. The coordinator spends a turn on each nudge.

friction.title: A manager stops on a harness permission block and the coordinator does not know
friction.decision: Fixed in 29-message-marker (5c8f6846): Claude Code and Codex spawns launch with the bypass flag, each hive message starts with the marker, and a manager sends a blocked record before it stops.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, the coordinator sent `manager-stenographer` (Claude Code, auto
mode) two inbox records. Record 3 relayed a user statement: the real-machine
acceptance of dev is verified. Record 4 asked for a read-only architecture
report. The auto-mode permission check blocked the memory write for record 3
as instruction poisoning, because the user statement came only through the
inbox. It also blocked a read-only `git ls-files` for record 4. The manager
asked the user two questions in its own pane and ended its turn. It sent no
inbox record to the coordinator. herdr showed the pane as `done`, and the
supervisor sends no nudge for a `quiet` record. Thus the coordinator saw no
stop. The user found the stop by hand in the manager tab.

Two causes:
1. The harness permission check treats an inbox record as untrusted input. A
   user statement or an approved goal that the coordinator relays does not
   authorize an action for the harness.
2. The manager instructions do not tell a manager to send a record to the
   coordinator when it stops for a user decision.

**Resolution 2026-10-19:**
Fixed in 29-message-marker, landed at 5c8f6846. Hive starts each spawned Claude
Code agent with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and each Codex agent with
`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`. The user approved these flags
directly. Each message that hive types into an agent pane (first prompt,
`hive agent send`, supervisor nudge) starts with `⬢ `. The role instructions
say that a `⬢` message came from hive, that a message without it came from the
user, and that the marker does not widen a grant. The manager skill and the
project template tell a manager to send the coordinator one record before it
stops for a user decision or on a harness block.

The fix was used before it landed: the auto-mode check of `manager-hive`
blocked the spawn of this task's worker with `[Create Unsafe Agents]`. The
manager sent the coordinator a blocked record and stopped, and the user
approved in the manager pane.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a Claude Code manager in auto mode.
2. Send it `hive inbox send --to manager-ID TEXT` with a user statement that
   it must record, or with a report goal.
3. Read the manager pane. The permission check blocks the action, and the
   manager asks the user in its pane.
4. Run `hive inbox --role coordinator`. No record from the manager is present.

friction.title: Manager spawn fails with `agent_pane_busy` right after `workspace.create`
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-18 the first `hive agent spawn --role manager --project
hive --harness claude --model claude-opus-5-5` in a home with no manager
workspace failed with `first tab busy: stop the agent or pass --pane`. The log
shows `workspace.create` at 22:34:09.993 and `agent.start` on the new root pane
at 22:34:10.003, ten milliseconds later. herdr answered `agent_pane_busy`:
`agent target pane wBD:p1 is not an available shell`. The shell of the new
pane was not ready. The spawn kept the workspace `wBD` and its project record,
and it marked the agent record `exited`. A second identical spawn one minute
later adopted `wBD` and started the manager. The error text names a wrong cause:
no agent held the pane. It occurred on each first spawn of a project manager:
twice in two attempts on 2026-10-18, for `hive` and for `stenographer`. The
retry succeeded each time. During rc-file startup, the shell runs commands in
its own process group. Thus, a group ID equal to the shell PID is not sufficient.
Commit `aa29b8d9` also requires one foreground process whose PID is the shell
PID.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Register a project with no manager workspace record.
2. Run `hive agent spawn --role manager --project ID --harness claude --model claude-opus-5-5`.
3. Read `.hive/logs/<date>.jsonl`: `agent.start` follows `workspace.create` within a few milliseconds and herdr returns `agent_pane_busy`.
4. Run the same spawn again: it adopts the workspace and succeeds.

friction.title: No hive path repairs a verified task
friction.decision: Fixed in 18-task-reopen (4f2bd6a5): hive task reopen moves a verified task to assigned, keeps the old check in verification_history, and land needs a new pass verify.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, `hive land --task 12-friction-log --mode merge`
failed with a merge conflict in `testdata/ste-baseline.json`. Task 11 landed
first, and each task added one baseline line. The task had the status
`verified`. `hive agent spawn --role worker` refused it with `task is
verified`. `hive task assign` refused it with `invalid transition: verified ->
assign`. The workaround was a Pi agent that the manager started by hand with
`herdr agent start` in a new tab of the task workspace. That agent merged
`origin/dev` into the task branch, kept both lines, ran the gate, and pushed.
Then `hive land` passed. The repair has no hive agent record and no second
verification record.

On 2026-10-19 the same conflict occurred for 15-inbox-ownership, after
17-verifier-project and 16-quiet-no-nudge landed. The worker and verifier had
exited, and herdr had closed the task workspace. The manager made a workspace
with `herdr workspace create`, started `t15-merge-1` with `herdr agent start`,
and that agent merged `origin/dev` twice and pushed. That agent has no hive
record, so it sent its report with `--agent manager-hive`.

Resolution: wave 3 did not use the reopen path. Task 19 landed first with no conflict. Task 18 then failed its verify, so it was assigned, not verified, and the respawned worker `t18-worker-2` merged `origin/dev` during the repair. First live use, 2026-10-19: 22-task-edit-brief was verified, and `hive land` failed with `merge conflict: testdata/ste-baseline.json` after 23-verify-clean-branch landed. The land left the home checkout clean. `hive task reopen --task 22-task-edit-brief --reason TEXT` moved the task to `assigned`, set `verification` to null, and put the old check in `verification_history` (1 item). `hive agent spawn --role worker --task 22-task-edit-brief` with no `--name` and no `--pane` made `t22-worker-2`, set it as the acting agent, and reopened the workspace. It got its first prompt. It merged `origin/dev` (10b5b191) and pushed c2374641. The fresh verifier `t22-verifier-2` recorded a pass, and `hive land` merged 77cdf44d. No hand step was needed.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Make two tasks that each add one line at the same place in a file.
2. Verify both tasks. Land the first task.
3. Run `hive land` for the second task. The merge fails with a conflict.
4. Run `hive agent spawn --role worker` for the second task. Hive returns
   `task is verified`.
5. Run `hive task assign` for the second task. Hive returns
   `invalid transition: verified -> assign`.

friction.title: Shell-ready race in worker and verifier spawns
friction.body:
**Summary:**
A worker or verifier spawn in a fresh worktree workspace could hit
`agent_pane_busy`. Commit `aa29b8d9` adds the shell-ready wait before the shared
`agent.start` call. This resolves the race for both roles.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Before commit `aa29b8d9`, create a fresh worktree workspace.
2. Spawn a worker or verifier in its root pane.
3. Check the log for `agent.start` before the shell is ready.
4. Check for `agent_pane_busy`.

friction.title: No `hive task edit --brief` command
friction.decision: Fixed in 22-task-edit-brief (77cdf44d): hive task edit --task ID --brief FILE, only for created or assigned, only by the controlling role.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
The manager changed a task brief by hand in
`.hive/state/briefs/` on 2026-10-18. hive has no `hive task edit --brief`
command. The manager must edit the stored brief by hand.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Run `hive task --help`.
2. Check that the command list has no `edit` command.
3. Edit a task brief in `.hive/state/briefs/` by hand.

friction.title: A verifier spawn with `--pane` requires `--project`
friction.decision: Fixed in 17-verifier-project (e7031497): hive derives the project from the task, and the docs are fixed.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
The manager skill shows a verifier spawn without `--project`. A
verifier spawn with `--pane` requires `--project`.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Read the verifier spawn command in `hive-manager/SKILL.md`.
2. Add `--pane PANE`. Do not add `--project`.
3. Run the command.
4. Check that hive requires `--project`.

friction.title: A verifier can record a verdict without a pushed VERIFIED.md
friction.decision: Fixed in 23-verify-clean-branch (27a883e9): hive task verify refuses a dirty worktree or an unpushed branch, and the verifier commits and pushes VERIFIED.md first.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, `t18-verifier-2` ran `hive task verify` with a pass for
18-task-reopen, and the task became `verified`. The new pass `VERIFIED.md`
stayed uncommitted in the worktree. The branch still held the old fail
`VERIFIED.md` of `t18-verifier-1`. A land at that point would put a fail
record on `dev`. The manager saw it in `git status` of the worktree and told
the verifier to commit and push (75f8c6e2). The same day, `t19-verifier-1`
left corrected V1-V3 evidence uncommitted in the 19-worker-respawn worktree.
After the land, `hive worktree remove` refused with `worktree is dirty`.
`hive task verify` and `hive land` do not check that the branch holds a
committed `VERIFIED.md` with the same verdict.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Let a verifier write `VERIFIED.md` and run `hive task verify` with no commit.
2. Check that the task status is `verified`.
3. Run `git status` in the worktree. `VERIFIED.md` is modified.
4. Run `hive land`. Hive does not refuse it.

friction.title: A verify fail leaves no workspace and no verifier for a re-verify
friction.decision: By design. The manager skill fix landed in 17-verifier-project (e7031497): after a verify fail, spawn a fresh verifier with no --pane.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, `t11-verifier-1` recorded a fail for
11-ci-workflow. Then the verifier stopped, and the supervisor closed the
worker workspace `wCK` when its last agent finished. After the repair,
`hive agent send` to the verifier returned `agent is stopped`, and
`herdr tab create --workspace wCK` returned `workspace_not_found`. The
workaround was a fresh verifier spawn with no `--pane`, which made the new
workspace `wCN` on the same worktree.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a worker and a verifier for a task in the same workspace.
2. Let the verifier record a fail and finish.
3. Repair the task and complete it again.
4. Run `hive agent send` to the verifier. Hive returns `agent is stopped`.
5. Run `herdr tab create --workspace ID` for the task workspace. herdr
   returns `workspace_not_found`.

friction.title: A verify fail leaves no workspace for the repair worker
friction.decision: Fixed in 19-worker-respawn (78381ba1): the spawn reopens the worktree workspace with worktree.open and updates the record.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, `t16-verifier-1` recorded a fail for 16-quiet-no-nudge. The
verifier ran in `wD6:p1`, the root pane of the task workspace, after the worker
`t16-worker-1` exited. `hive agent stop --agent t16-verifier-1` closed `wD6`.
The task record still named `wD6:p1` as the worktree pane. Then
`hive agent spawn --role worker --task 16-quiet-no-nudge` failed with
`worktree pane mismatch: pane_id`, and `hive worktree create --task
16-quiet-no-nudge` failed with `task has a worktree`. The workaround was
`herdr workspace create --cwd WORKTREE --label 16-quiet-no-nudge`, then a
worker spawn with `--pane` and `--project`. The task record kept
`t16-worker-1` as the acting agent, so the brief told the repair worker to run
`hive task complete --agent t16-worker-1`. The fresh-verifier rule of wave 2
covers the re-verify. It does not cover the repair worker.

`hive task complete --agent t16-worker-1` then failed with `agent not found:
t16-worker-1`, because that agent was stopped. The fix was
`hive task assign --task 16-quiet-no-nudge --agent t16-worker-2` by the
manager. Then `hive task complete --agent t16-worker-2` passed.

Resolution: Live check 2026-10-19: after a verify fail on 18-task-reopen, `hive agent spawn --role worker --task 18-task-reopen` with no `--name` and no `--pane` picked `t18-worker-2`, set it as the acting agent, and reopened the task workspace `wDJ` on the same worktree.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Spawn a worker for a task. Let it complete and exit.
2. Spawn a verifier with no `--pane`. Hive puts it in the task workspace.
3. Let the verifier record a fail. Run `hive agent stop` for the verifier.
4. Check that herdr closed the task workspace.
5. Run `hive agent spawn --role worker` for the task with no `--pane`. Hive
   returns `worktree pane mismatch: pane_id`.
6. Run `hive worktree create` for the task. Hive returns `task has a worktree`.

friction.title: A worker spawn into an assigned task keeps the old acting agent
friction.decision: Fixed in 19-worker-respawn (78381ba1): the spawn sets the acting agent and refuses while the old worker is live.
friction.body:
**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, the manager spawned `t11-worker-2` with
`hive agent spawn --role worker --pane` to repair 11-ci-workflow after a
verify fail. The task still named `t11-worker-1` as the acting agent.
`hive task complete` from `t11-worker-2` failed with `not the acting agent`.
The workaround was `hive task assign --task 11-ci-workflow --agent
t11-worker-2`, then `hive task complete`.

Resolution: Live check 2026-10-19: after a verify fail on 18-task-reopen, `hive agent spawn --role worker --task 18-task-reopen` with no `--name` and no `--pane` picked `t18-worker-2`, set it as the acting agent, and reopened the task workspace `wDJ` on the same worktree.

**Reproduction steps:**
1. Let a worker finish a task. Let the verifier record a fail.
2. Spawn a second worker for the same task with `--pane`.
3. In the second worker, run `hive task complete`.
4. Check that hive returns `not the acting agent`.

files.reference/dogfood/friction/entries/scrat:
---
title: "Bare hive in a scratch home starts real tabs"
status: "Open"
opened: 2026-10-20
decision: "Task 8-no-startup adds the opt-in switch --no-startup and HIVE_NO_STARTUP=1"
---

**Summary:**
Bare hive runs the startup of G9: in herdr, it starts a
coordinator and a supervisor in their own tabs when they are
missing. A worker or verifier that runs bare hive with
HIVE_HOME set to a scratch home gets no live coordinator and a
stale supervisor claim, so each run starts a new coordinator
tab and a new hive supervise process in the caller workspace.

**Reproduction:**
1. In a herdr pane, make a scratch home with a marker.
2. Run HIVE_HOME=<scratch> hive and quit the TUI.
3. herdr tab list shows a new coordinator and supervisor tab.

**Occurrences:**
2026-10-20  worker of 101 left 4 supervisors, 8 tabs
2026-10-20  t91-worker-1 closed the user TUI tab
2026-10-21  third scratch hive tab leak

**Mitigation:**
Task 8-no-startup of feature tui-v2 adds the switch
hive --no-startup and the variable HIVE_NO_STARTUP=1, from
decision 34 of the spec. With either one, bare hive opens the
TUI. It makes no tab, starts no coordinator and no supervisor,
and does not rename the tab.
The worker skill and the verifier skill tell each agent to run
bare hive only with the switch or the variable.

**Summary:**
On 2026-10-19, the supervisor (pid 1718014) started at 13:22
from the hive binary of 72a33b5b. The managers rebuilt
~/go/bin/hive after waves 2, 3, and 4. The supervisor kept the
old code, so the wave 2 change was not live. hive doctor
reported the supervisor as live and did not compare its binary
with the installed one.

**Resolved by:**
3-tui-restart  merge 3ccd93fb

**Reproduction:**
1. Start hive supervise.
2. Land a change to the supervisor and run go install or
   go build for hive.
3. Run hive doctor. It reports the old supervisor as live.
4. Trigger the changed behavior. The supervisor uses the old
   code.
No skill told an agent to restart the supervisor after a
rebuild.
